definitions.gloss: deep-fried thin tofu; fried tofu pouch
definitions.explanation: Thin slices of tofu that have been deep-fried until golden and puffy. Has a distinctive texture - crispy outside, spongy inside - that absorbs flavors well.

examples.japanese: {味噌汁|みそしる}に{油揚|あぶらあ}げを{入|い}れる。
examples.english: Add fried tofu to the miso soup.

examples.japanese: {油揚|あぶらあ}げを{開|ひら}いていなり{寿司|ずし}を{作|つく}る。
examples.english: Open the fried tofu pouches to make inari sushi.

examples.japanese: {油揚|あぶらあ}げは{油抜|あぶらぬ}きしてから{使|つか}う。
examples.english: Remove excess oil from the fried tofu before using.

notes:
WORD STRUCTURE:
{油|あぶら} (oil) + {揚|あ}げ (deep-frying)

Literally "oil-fried" - tofu that has been deep-fried.

PREPARATION:
{油抜|あぶらぬ}き (removing excess oil) is often done by:
- Pouring boiling water over the tofu
- Briefly blanching in hot water
This removes excess oil and helps it absorb other flavors.

COMMON USES:
・{味噌汁|みそしる} - miso soup
・いなり{寿司|ずし} - inari sushi (sushi rice stuffed in sweetened pouches)
・きつねうどん - udon with fried tofu
・{煮物|にもの} - simmered dishes
・{炊|た}き{込|こ}みご{飯|はん} - mixed rice

VARIATIONS:
・{油揚|あぶらあ}げ - thin fried tofu
・{厚揚|あつあ}げ - thick fried tofu (different texture)

CULTURAL NOTE:
In Shinto folklore, foxes ({狐|きつね}) are believed to love {油揚|あぶらあ}げ. This is why "きつね" dishes (like きつねうどん) contain fried tofu.
